; closure-lines.fk — read a line of an fkwu closure back to the unit that wrote it.
;
; `./fkwu --closure <unit> <out>` joins every unit of a closure into one plain-Form
; file and heads each unit's text with a line "; unit: <path>". A sibling kernel

goal: form/form-stdlib/closure-lines.fk reads a line of an fkwu closure back to the unit that wrote it. A closure is text whose lines are separated by byte 10; each unit's text follows a marker line that begins with the eight bytes "; unit: " followed by the unit's path. Add four new definitions inside the (do ...), before the final 0. (defn cl-marker? (s at) (eq (str_find s "; unit: " at) at)) is true when the line starting at byte at is a marker. (defn cl-line-end (s at) ...) lets e be (str_find s (byte_to_str 10) at) and answers (str_len s) when (lt e 0), else e. (defn cl-walk (s at line want unit start) ...) walks the lines: it answers (nothing) when (ge at (str_len s)); otherwise it lets end be (cl-line-end s at) and mark be (cl-marker? s at); when (eq line want) it answers (nothing) if mark is true or unit is (nothing), else (list unit (sub line start)); when line is not want it goes on with (cl-walk s (add end 1) (add line 1) want next-unit next-start), where next-unit is (substring s (add at 8) end) and next-start is line when mark is true, and unit and start unchanged when it is false. (defn cl-unit-at (text line) (cl-walk text 0 1 line (nothing) 0)) answers (list path n): the path on the nearest marker line above line and n the number of lines below that marker. In Form a let is (let name value) inside a (do ...) whose last form is the answer, and every if has a then and an else. Leave the header comment and the final 0 exactly as they are; the new code is new definitions only.

goal: form/form-stdlib/sort.fk is the body's one sort home (its preludes line loads core.fk, which gives len, div, reverse-onto and nothing). Add these definitions inside the (do ...), before the final 0. (defn sort-take (xs n) ...) answers the first n items: (list) when (nil? xs) or (eq n 0), else (cons (head xs) (sort-take (tail xs) (sub n 1))). (defn sort-drop (xs n) ...) answers xs without its first n items: xs when (nil? xs) or (eq n 0), else (sort-drop (tail xs) (sub n 1)). (defn sort-before? (le? key a b) ...) answers (le? a b) when key is (nothing), else (le? key a b). (defn sort-merge (le? key xs ys acc) ...) answers (reverse-onto acc ys) when (nil? xs), (reverse-onto acc xs) when (nil? ys), and otherwise conses the head of xs onto acc and goes on with (tail xs) when (sort-before? le? key (head xs) (head ys)), else conses the head of ys and goes on with (tail ys); taking from xs on ties is what keeps the sort stable. (defn sort-with (le? key xs) ...) answers xs when (nil? xs) or (nil? (tail xs)); otherwise it lets h be (div (len xs) 2) and answers (sort-merge le? key (sort-with le? key (sort-take xs h)) (sort-with le? key (sort-drop xs h)) (list)). (defn sort-int-le? (a b) (le a b)). (defn sort-str-le? (a b) (sort-str-le-at a b 0)) with (defn sort-str-le-at (a b i) ...) answering true when (ge i (str_len a)), false when (ge i (str_len b)), true when (lt (str_byte_at a i) (str_byte_at b i)), false when (gt (str_byte_at a i) (str_byte_at b i)), else (sort-str-le-at a b (add i 1)); never compare strings with lt, which stops. (defn sort-key-le? (key a b) (le (key a) (key b))). Then (defn sort-ints (xs) (sort-with sort-int-le? (nothing) xs)), (defn sort-strs (xs) (sort-with sort-str-le? (nothing) xs)) and (defn sort-by (xs key) (sort-with sort-key-le? key xs)). In Form a let is (let name value) inside a (do ...) whose last form is the answer, and every if has a then and an else. Leave the header comment, the preludes line and the final 0 exactly as they are; the new code is new definitions only.

form/form-stdlib/bml/host-walk.bml is the body's walk steps. Change these two definitions inside the HostWalk class.

def hw-conflicted?(sync) = ...
Answers true when the sync text names a conflict with at least one file, and false otherwise. It must not answer true for a bare "conflict:" with no file name after it. The definition must check that the text after "conflict:" on that line, trimmed, is not empty.

def hw-held-turns(sync) { ... }
Answers 0. It prints a [walk] line that names what was found in the sync text. When hw-conflicted?(sync) is true, the line must say the branch could not follow main and name the conflict files (the text after "conflict:" on that line, trimmed). When hw-conflicted?(sync) is false, the line must say the branch could not follow main and name the sync text as a rebase refusal. The definition must call hw-conflicted?(sync) to decide which shape to print.

Leave every other definition in the file exactly as it is.
